_about: Coarse BLE advertisement signatures for device_class / is_tracker. Presence-based only: a signature matches when the named company ID, Apple Continuity TLV type, or 16-bit service UUID is PRESENT in a device's adverts. Nothing inside an advert is decoded beyond listing which TLV types and service UUIDs appear. No owner identification (spec R8). Extend by adding entries; no code change needed.

_match_keys.company_id: manufacturer-data company ID (first 2 bytes, little-endian), e.g. '0x004C'
_match_keys.apple_type: an Apple Continuity TLV type byte present inside 0x004C manufacturer data (TLVs are type/length/value)
_match_keys.service_uuid16: a 16-bit service UUID present either in the advertised service UUIDs or as a service-data key

_confidence: high = the match is tracker-specific and confirmed by a primary source; med = the UUID/type is registered to a company that makes only trackers, or is named a tracker by the project spec; low = the UUID is registered company-wide and may also appear on non-tracker products.

_deferred.google_find_my_network: The build spec seeds Google Find My Network as a tracker family, but it is NOT implemented here, on purpose. A correct coarse match needs the specific service UUID the Find My Device Network advertises, and that is not established by any source on this machine. The Google-owned 16-bit UUIDs actually seen in the captures (0xFEF3, and generally 0xFEAA Eddystone / 0xFE2C Fast Pair per data/bluetooth-sig/member_uuids.yaml) are NOT the Find My Device Network identifier: flagging them as a tracker would mark every Google Fast Pair / Eddystone device as a tracker (the same company-wide false-positive avoided for Samsung 0x0075). Add an entry only once the FMDN UUID is confirmed against a cited primary source. Raised with the maintainer at the stage-2 gate.

signatures.notes: Apple Continuity TLV type 0x12 is the offline-finding (Find My) message. It is broadcast by ANY Apple device participating in Find My (iPhone, AirPods, AirTag, third-party Find My accessories), so this flags 'a Find My advert is present', NOT specifically an AirTag. Nothing in the TLV value is decoded, so separated-from-owner vs near-owner state is not distinguished. Find My addresses rotate, so the same physical tracker appears under many addresses over time.
